title: Weight Averaging for Out-of-Distribution Generalization and Few-Shot Domain Adaptation
publication_status_observed: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2501.08361v1, 14 Jan 2025); originally an MSc thesis at EPFL (February 2023)
main_claims: Incorporating gradient similarity as a regularizer explicitly increases model diversity in weight averaging, improving OOD generalization performance.
Combining weight averaging (WA) and SAM leads to improved OOD generalization and significantly increased few-shot domain adaptation accuracy.
Weight averaging with gradient diversity (WA + SAM + grad) achieves the best in-distribution performance on CIFAR-100 (84.31%) compared to ERM, DiWA, and WA+Adam+grad.
methodology: The author proposes weight averaging with gradient similarity regularization: multiple models are trained from shared initialization with different hyperparameters, with a gradient similarity term (cosine similarity between model gradients) added to the loss to enforce diversity. The final model averages all trained weights. For few-shot domain adaptation, weight averaging is either applied before or after few-shot fine-tuning. Experiments use ImageNet-pretrained ResNet50 on PACS, VLCS (DomainBed), and CIFAR-100.
key_results: WA (SAM + grad) achieves 84.31% on CIFAR-100 vs. ERM baseline 79.54%, DiWA 84.12%, and WA (Adam + grad) 84.11%.
On PACS DomainBed, the method achieves best performance on the Cartoon domain and is comparable to DiWA with fewer averaged models.
Combining WA and SAM significantly increases few-shot domain adaptation accuracy on digits datasets (MNIST, SVHN, USPS, MNIST-M) and domain adaptation datasets (VLCS, PACS).
limitations: Experiments are limited to PACS and VLCS from DomainBed due to time and computation constraints; results on TerraIncognita, OfficeHome, and DomainNet are not provided.
The thesis does not provide ablation on the relative contributions of gradient diversity vs. SAM in the combined method.
The thesis-level work lacks rigorous statistical comparisons and the paper is a repost of an MSc thesis, not a peer-reviewed publication.
relevance_to_rq: Supporting relevance to the RQ's weight_averaging sub-topic: this work directly combines SWA/weight averaging with SAM for OOD generalization, showing complementary benefits. It uses DomainBed benchmarks rather than CIFAR-C corruptions, but the finding that WA+SAM outperforms either alone is relevant context for our flat-minima comparison.
